punchline: Elephants responded to an alarm call played only through the soil, while microphones above ground heard nothing.
thirty_sec: In Etosha, researchers took a recording of a herd's alarm calls and turned it into vibrations in the ground. Microphones above the soil heard nothing, yet elephants at a waterhole reacted. They answered nearby recordings more than far ones, and the experiments suggest elephants may feel each other from around two kilometres away.
